Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto, titled "For a Fair Deal," presents a comprehensive vision for transforming British politics and addressing what they describe as years of Conservative neglect across healthcare, the economy, environment, and public services.

## Key Themes

### Economy
The party pledges responsible fiscal management while investing in green infrastructure and renewable energy. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, reforming capital gains tax, increasing the Digital Services Tax on tech giants, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. They commit to fixing the UK-EU trading relationship and supporting small businesses through expanded access to capital.

### Healthcare
The NHS receives significant focus, with promises to guarantee GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Other commitments include guaranteeing NHS dental access for emergency care, placing mental health professionals in every school, boosting cancer survival rates with a 62-day treatment guarantee, and investing in public health to help people live five more healthy years.

### Social Care
The manifesto proposes free personal care based on Scotland's model, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, establishing a Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard minimum wage), and providing statutory respite breaks for unpaid carers. A cross-party commission would develop sustainable long-term funding.

### Environment
Climate commitments include achieving net zero by 2045, generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030, and launching an emergency home insulation programme. The party pledges to tackle the sewage scandal by transforming water companies into public benefit companies, banning executive bonuses until pollution ends, and replacing Ofwat with a stronger regulator.

### Housing
Targets include building 380,000 homes annually (150,000 social homes), banning no-fault evictions, creating three-year default tenancies, abolishing residential leaseholds, and ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

### Political Reform
Democratic reforms include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, capping political donations, reforming the House of Lords, and enshrining the Ministerial Code in law.

### International Affairs
The party advocates fixing EU relations through a four-stage roadmap ultimately aiming for Single Market membership, supporting Ukraine, returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, and advocating for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire with a two-state solution.

# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The Green Party's 2024 manifesto presents a vision for a "fairer, greener country" during ongoing cost-of-living and climate crises. Co-leaders Carla Denyer and Adrian Ramsay argue that climate action and social fairness are interconnected solutions.

## Key Policy Areas

### Health and Social Care
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Priorities include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, restoring NHS dentistry (£3bn annually), boosting staff pay, and protecting the NHS from privatisation. For social care, they propose free personal care, increased carer pay, and £20bn annual investment.

### Housing
The manifesto commits to 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a major home insulation programme (£29bn over five years) to reduce energy bills.

### Energy and Climate
The party would halt new fossil fuel extraction, end oil and gas subsidies, and aim for wind to provide 70% of electricity by 2030. They oppose nuclear power and support community energy ownership. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would fund the green transition.

### Economy and Work
Proposals include £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership, a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and restoring trade union rights. They would tax wealth fairly, including a wealth tax on assets above £10m.

### Welfare and Cost of Living
The party would increase Universal Credit by £40 weekly, abolish the two-child benefit cap, end the five-week benefit wait, increase disability benefits by 5%, and work toward Universal Basic Income.

### Education
Commitments include £8bn school investment, free school meals for all children, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, abolishing Ofsted, and £5bn for SEND provision.

### Transport
Plans include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, free bus travel for under-18s, railway renationalisation, £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure, and ending new road building.

### Environment and Nature
The manifesto proposes a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, water company nationalisation, and £1.5bn additional DEFRA funding.

### Democracy and Rights
Proposals include proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords, defending human rights legislation, and supporting trans rights including self-ID.

### International Affairs
The party calls for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI.

## Funding
Revenue would come from wealth taxes (estimated £50-70bn annually), carbon taxes (up to £80bn by parliament's end), and business tax reforms. The party accepts increased borrowing for green investment, rejecting conventional fiscal rules while monitoring inflation risks.
